title: Market for cars
questionText: Consider the market for cars, which letter represents producer surplus?
explanation: Producer surplus is the area between the price and the supply curve — the gap between what producers receive and their lowest acceptable price. Here that is region B.

title: Market for cars
explanation: Consumer surplus is the area between the demand curve and the price — the gap between what consumers would pay and what they do pay. Here that is region A.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Suppose that the price of cars is at a disequilibrium price of $52,000. Which letters now represent the consumer surplus?
explanation: At the higher disequilibrium price consumers pay more, so consumer surplus shrinks to the triangle above the price and below demand — region A.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letters represent the new amount of producer surplus?
explanation: At the higher price producers earn more per unit on the quantity actually traded, so producer surplus is the area B + C.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letters represent the deadweight loss?
explanation: Because trade is below the efficient quantity, the mutually beneficial trades that no longer happen are lost — the deadweight loss, regions D + E.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Suppose that the government impose a tax on Cars due to negative externalities. From the diagram shown what is the per unit size of the tax?
explanation: The per-unit tax is the vertical distance between the original supply curve and the S+tax curve — $24,000 per car.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letter(s) now represent consumer surplus?
explanation: The tax raises the price consumers pay, shrinking consumer surplus to the triangle above that price — region A.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letter(s) now represent producer surplus?
explanation: The tax lowers the price producers keep, shrinking producer surplus to the area below that price and above supply — region F.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letters represent tax revenue for the government?
explanation: Tax revenue is the per-unit tax times the quantity still traded — the rectangle B + C.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letters represent the deadweight loss?
explanation: The tax reduces trade below the efficient quantity; the lost gains from trade are the deadweight loss, regions D + E.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Suppose the government imposes a quota limiting the number of cars that can be sold to 25,000. Which letter(s) represent the new consumer surplus?
explanation: The quota raises the price consumers pay, so consumer surplus falls to the triangle above that price — region A.

title: Market for cars
questionText: Which letters represent the new level of producer surplus?
explanation: With sales capped at 25,000 and a higher price, producer surplus is the area B + C.

title: Market for cars
questionText: What letters represent the deadweight loss?
explanation: The quota cuts trade below the efficient quantity, so the lost gains from trade — the deadweight loss — are regions D + E.
